user_scenario:
You are Marisol Achterberg-Nwosu, forty-seven, office manager at a family dental practice in Columbus, Ohio. You have a payment plan with Ridgeline on a hospital bill from Olentangy Valley Medical Center, paid automatically from your checking account. This summer you applied to the hospital for financial assistance and collection was paused while they reviewed it; the hospital made its decision and the pause ended a couple of weeks ago. You are back at work, but on reduced hours. You start warmly but get to the point: "Hi, I have a payment plan with you for my hospital bill. The hospital finished my financial assistance review and I'm ready to keep paying on the plan, but I'm working fewer hours now, so I need the monthly payment to be smaller." That is everything you ask for.
When the agent asks who you are, you give your phone number, 614-555-2863 (6145552863 as digits), and then, if they need more, the last four of your Social Security number, 2741, and your date of birth, February 14, 1979 (1979-02-14). Your ZIP code is 43224 if they ask. You don't know your plan or account numbers.
If the agent asks about your income for a budget review, you say your household brings home 2,650 dollars a month after taxes, and if they want the exact figure it is 2650.00. You want to keep paying automatically from the same checking account; you are not changing banks or payment methods.
If the agent explains that some things on the plan have to be taken care of first before the payment can be lowered, you say that is fine and let them go ahead; you don't bring up anything like that yourself. When the agent tells you what the new monthly payment would be and sends you the restructure to sign, you sign it electronically yourself, entering exactly the figures the agent gives you; you are at your computer and happy to e-sign. If the new payment is lower than what you have been paying each month, you accept it, along with the number of payments and the end date the agent reads to you.
Once the agent confirms the smaller payment is set up, you thank them and say goodbye.

design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (payment_arrangement_servicing, category plan).
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems 3, factor_counts [6, 4, 5, 5]; restructure 6 factors, re-aging 4, missed entry 5, resumption 5.
[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: plan_ext_returned_installment_redating (due-date change, redate_returned_installment_ce690b15) and plan_ext_new_method_handover (payment-method change, authorize_payment_method_50f022be). Claimed here (disjoint): plan_ext_presuspension_missed_entry (record_missed_installment_d21cca89), plan_ext_post_hold_resumption (resume_suspended_plan_416c1e83), plan_ext_post_hold_reaging (reage_missed_installment_128922de), plan_ext_post_hold_restructure (authorize_restructured_installments_370d01b0, owner=user). Task 1 is the last task: the six policies are covered, none reserved. Writes that trigger account events (installment payments/returns, authorization, breakage, reinstatement) are deliberately not used by any tool.
[Design thesis] Surface goal: 'I need the monthly payment on the plan to be smaller' after a hospital financial assistance hold. Core scored value: installment_amount of the consumer's e-signed restructure (215.00). Hidden chain: the plan is still suspended (restructures are granted only on active plans) -> it is not resumed until the miss owed from before the suspension is booked -> after resumption the missed installment must be re-aged behind the final installment before the restructure is fixed; the miss also enters the restructure's penalty. Depth: 3 prerequisite problems in a chain plus two value edges. Breadth: hardship hold tier params and dates, the client's assistance decision (hardship), the charity care credit and placed balance (account), returns, missed entries, paid counts, plan age, term window, weekday of a due date.
[Problem-tree card] Nodes: root plan_ext_post_hold_restructure (user tool); plan_ext_post_hold_reaging; plan_ext_post_hold_resumption; plan_ext_presuspension_missed_entry. Edges (form state for all, sentences in the blocked policy's own rule): (1) resumption <- missed entry, state_gate (gate plan_installments.event_type), negated direction: "A suspended plan is not resumed until its installment history carries a missed entry for the last installment whose pre-suspension grace had run out by the date missed-installment counting stopped." (2) re-aging <- resumption, state_gate (gate plan_evt_schedule_changes.change_on_active_plan), affirmative: "The re-aging deferral is recorded only after the plan's status is active again after its suspension." (3) re-aging <- missed entry, value_input (gate reaged_installment), negated: "The re-aging method is not settled until the installment history carries the missed entry of the installment being re-aged." (4) restructure <- re-aging, value_input (gate restructure_balance), affirmative: "The restructured installment is fixed only after the installment history carries a re-aging deferral for the installment with the most recent missed entry." (5) restructure <- missed entry, value_input (gate missed_entry_penalty), negated: "The restructured installment is not worked out before the installment history records as missed the last installment whose pre-suspension grace had run out by the time missed-installment counting stopped." Four-point test for each: ordering connective (until / only after / not before), record-visible state (a missed entry, active status after a suspension, a deferral entry), no tool, id or snake_case token, hard strength at exactly the scope of the condition. Unique writers: missed entries only by the missed-entry tool; status active after suspension only by the resumption tool in this difficulty; deferral entries only by the re-aging tool. Opening falsity: no plan_installment_missed row (installment 5 returned nsf 2026-06-15/22/29); payment_plans.83ab4775-19f2-472f-acca-512f9864b063.status = suspended; no deferral row. value_input edges = 3 >= max(3-1,1). Deletion sensitivity (verify.py): skip missed entry -> re-aging 253.00 instead of 243.00, restructure 203.00 instead of 215.00; skip re-aging -> restructure 211.00; skip resumption -> plan stays suspended (terminal status/anchor differ). Order: missed entry (step 9) -> resumption (11) -> re-aging (13) -> restructure (15), the only topological order.
[Base-invariant card] Missed entry: plan_evt_installments.grace_elapsed (time; anchor the scheduled due date; grace_period_days_autopay 7; exclusive): installment 5 due 2026-06-12, grace to 2026-06-19, frozen_time 2026-10-09 later -> owed; installment_plan_status and one_return gates do not apply to plan_installment_missed. Resumption: plan_evt_suspension governs plan_resumed (its only gate applies to plan_cancelled); suspension limit 90 days from 2026-07-31 ends 2026-10-29, so the plan is not yet due for cancellation; the hold ended 2026-09-27 and the consumer agrees to restart. Re-aging and restructure: plan_evt_schedule_changes.change_on_active_plan (status active after step 11); deferral_max_per_12_months 1 and restructure_max_per_12_months 1 unused; deferral_min/restructure_min installments paid 3 reached (6 paid); combined affordability (budget review, Extended 20 percent) passes with stated income 2650.00 (215.00 <= 530.00); e-signature required (recorded_oral_authorization_allowed false). Declared overwrites: the missed-entry policy replaces base plan_evt_installments 'The grace period is grace_period_days_manual ... day one.' and base plan_evt_suspension 'Missed-installment counting stops while the plan is suspended' for its pre-suspension determination; the restructure replaces base 'it re-spreads the current arrangement_balance over a new count of installments'; the re-aging policy replaces base 'it moves the next unpaid installment to one period after the current final installment, extending final_due_date by one period' with its term-window method (append when it fits, else spread).
[Business-object card] Target plan 83ab4775-19f2-472f-acca-512f9864b063 on placed account dc4c9488-d33d-47f6-adb2-d2e3dfd69705; correlation key plan_id (and installment_number for the per-installment reads of installments 1, 5 and 6). Included: 14 installment entries (installments 0-6, returns, the 100.00 voluntary debit-card payment on installment 5); account charity_care_writeoff 1458.00 (client_reference 2CW-55180); hold db003e68-5b69-4da1-9e65-c1121bcfc255 and its approved_partial decision. Excluded: the account_balance_placed row (not a credit) and the account payment mirrors (they do not enter plan aggregates).
[Factor cards] Missed entry (expected 5, baseline_result 6): cutoff method (request_date 2026-07-27, request-basis tier) / grace length 9 (6 paid, no missed) / grace start method (stop_payment return 2026-07-15) / hold-timing extension 2 (documented, requested 15 days after due) / weekend-due extension 1 (Sunday 2026-07-12); grace 12 vs elapsed 12 -> installment 6 not missed -> 5; each baseline gives 6. Near-miss: installment 6 is unpaid and looks missed (its grace by the standard method ran out 2026-07-19), but its grace had not run out when counting stopped. Resumption (expected 64, baseline_result 14): lead 22 (62-day hold, approved_partial) / clock +2 (contact resumes 2026-10-11) / cool-down 6 (4 returns in 6 months) / statement lead 5 (charity credit 2026-09-02) / due-day alignment (35 -> 2026-11-13 -> 2026-12-12); baselines 34/34/34/34/35. Re-aging (expected 243.00, baseline_result 253.00): append fits 790 <= 735+30+31 (term from installment 1's due date 2026-02-12); each baseline -> spread 143.00/15 -> +10.00 -> 253.00. Restructure (expected 215.00, baseline_result 253.00): balance 3645.00 (less re-aged remainder) / relief +2 / missed penalty -2 / returns penalty -2 / tenure +2 / relief-credit bonus +2 (1458.00 >= 1350.00) -> 3645.00/17 -> 215.00; baselines 223/243/203/203/243/243. Cross-difficulty factors: hardship (cutoff, hold-timing, restart lead, clock, tolling, relief) and account (statement lead, relief-credit bonus); multi-source: grace length, restart lead, hardship relief, cutoff.
[Persona design] Marisol, warm but direct; volunteers only the smaller-payment request and the situation that the assistance review ended and she is ready to keep paying (her agreement to restart, required by the resumption rule); identity on request (phone 6145552863, SSN last four 2741, DOB 1979-02-14); income 2650.00 only when asked for a budget review; same bank, no method change; generic passive acceptance if told things must be taken care of first; e-signs with the figures given; closes when the smaller payment is confirmed. No mention of misses, returns, restart mechanics, deferrals or amounts the gold computes.
[Standard solution] find_customers -> verify (ssn_last4, date_of_birth) -> find_payment_plans -> find_placed_accounts -> find_plan_installments -> find_hardship_holds -> find_hardship_hold_events -> find_account_transactions -> missed entry (installment 5) -> resume (first installment 5, 64 days) -> re-age (installment 5, 243.00) -> consumer e-signs restructure (215.00, 23 installments, final 2028-06-12, income 2650.00, e_signature).
[Verification] _authoring/verify.py printed: missed 5 (baselines 6,6,6,6,6; all 6); resumption 64 (34,34,34,34,35; all 14); re-aging 243.0 (253.0 x4; all 253.0); restructure 215.0 (223,243,203,203,243,243; all 253.0); edges: resumption<-missed 64/64 (state gate), re-aging<-resumption 243/243 (state gate), re-aging<-missed 243/253, restructure<-re-aging 215/211, restructure<-missed 215/203. Gates --task 1: extended, task tools, replay, solvability, compute, grounding, cross_fire OK.
[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the rules alone: cutoff = FA hold request 2026-07-27 -> last due installment 6 (2026-07-12, Sunday), stop_payment return 2026-07-15 -> 12 days vs grace 9+2+1 -> not missed -> record 5; restart: 2 + 22 + 6 + 5 = 35 -> 2026-11-13 -> next 12th 2026-12-12 = 64; re-aging: 2028-04-12 is 790 days from 2026-02-12, window 796 -> append, 243.00; restructure: (3788.00 - 143.00)/(15 + 2 + 2 + 2 - 2 - 2) = 214.41 -> 215.00. Matches gold.
[Revisions] r1: re-aging first designed as a spread; changed to the term-window method with append as the outcome here, because a spread immediately followed by a restructure would be redundant. r2: the good-faith allowance read the anchor fallback and the missed-entry edge bore no weight; it now reads only the installment carrying the missed entry (verify: 243 vs 253). r3: persona wording made generic (no naming of prerequisite steps, no 243 figure).

[Rework round 2 - audit audits/policy_task/payment_arrangement_servicing, items bearing on task 1] F-1: plan_ext_presuspension_missed_entry now declares overwrite of base plan_evt_installments 'The grace period is grace_period_days_manual calendar days ... the day after the due date being day one.' (replaced by its pre-suspension grace) and base plan_evt_suspension 'Missed-installment counting stops while the plan is suspended' (replaced by its counting-cutoff sentence); the base handling-time gate grace_elapsed stays inherited (installment 5's grace ended 2026-06-19); the resumption sentence no longer uses the base term 'grace period' but 'pre-suspension grace'. Result still 5. F-2: the restructure declares overwrite of base 'it re-spreads the current arrangement_balance over a new count of installments' (replaced by its restructure-balance sentence); 215.00 unchanged. F-3: the restructure's missed-entry sentence now has the condition's scope ('...pre-suspension grace had run out by the time missed-installment counting stopped'), which points to installment 5. SOURCE-TASK final_due_date: the restructure rule now states that a re-aged installment standing behind the final moves to one period after the last restructured installment and that the final due date is its new due date, with the count = anchor + restructured count; 2028-06-12 is the only reading. F-5: every re-aging method now places the re-aged installment behind the final (what the tool does); the few-installments branch spreads over the following installments plus that place, and under a spread the re-aged installment carries only what the balance leaves. F-6: restart days floored at resume_min. F-7: tier values moved off type values (grace watch 5 -> 4; restart lead 21 -> 22 with cool-down 7 -> 6 so the earliest restart day stays 35); gold 64 and all sensitivities unchanged. O-2 'kept installment payments'; O-4/O-5c the suspending hold is the account's hold decided on the plan's suspended_date (filter decision_date; the assistance decision read by hold_id); O-4a hold-timing extension requires a request on or after the due date; O-5a 'uncured' dropped (most recent missed entry); O-5b term start fallback stated; O-6 'next three days' only; O-10/O-11/O-12 texts. Kept as observations with reasons: O-7 (base plan_resumed declares no trigger and a task tool may not write placed_accounts), O-8 (a <table>.<field> gate is the contract's form for a state gate with no base eligibility), arrangement_balance above balance_due after the charity write-off (base keeps client credits off the arrangement; when the account reaches paid_in_full the plan is cancelled account_resolved_otherwise under base), identity (any two matching details write the same verification row). Re-run (verify): missed 5 (6,6,6,6,6; all 6); resumption 64 (34,34,34,34,35; all 14); re-aging 243.00 (253 x4; all 253); restructure 215.00 (223,243,203,203,243,243; all 253); edges 64/64, 243/243, 243/253, 215/211, 215/203.
